verses.text: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight; and Yahweh delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
There was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and childless.
Yahweh’s angel appeared to the woman, and said to her, “See now, you are barren and childless; but you shall conceive, and bear a son.
Now therefore please beware and drink no wine nor strong drink, and don’t eat any unclean thing:

for, behold, you shall conceive, and give birth to a son. No razor shall come on his head; for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb. He shall begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.”

Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, “A man of God came to me, and his face was like the face of the angel of God, very awesome. I didn’t ask him where he was from, neither did he tell me his name;

but he said to me, ‘Behold, you shall conceive, and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink. Don’t eat any unclean thing; for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb to the day of his death.’”
Then Manoah entreated Yahweh, and said, “Oh, Lord, please let the man of God whom you sent come again to us, and teach us what we should do to the child who shall be born.”
God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman as she sat in the field, but Manoah, her husband, wasn’t with her.
The woman hurried and ran, and told her husband, and said to him, “Behold, the man who came to me that day has appeared to me,”
Manoah arose, and followed his wife, and came to the man, and said to him, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” He said, “I am.”
Manoah said, “Now let your words happen. What shall the child’s way of life and mission be?”
Yahweh’s angel said to Manoah, “Of all that I said to the woman let her beware.
She may not eat of anything that comes of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing. Let her observe all that I commanded her.”
Manoah said to Yahweh’s angel, “Please stay with us, that we may make a young goat ready for you.”
Yahweh’s angel said to Manoah, “Though you detain me, I won’t eat your bread. If you will prepare a burnt offering, you must offer it to Yahweh.” For Manoah didn’t know that he was Yahweh’s angel.
Manoah said to Yahweh’s angel, “What is your name, that when your words happen, we may honor you?”
Yahweh’s angel said to him, “Why do you ask about my name, since it is incomprehensible ?”
So Manoah took the young goat with the meal offering, and offered it on the rock to Yahweh. Then the angel did an amazing thing as Manoah and his wife watched.
For when the flame went up toward the sky from off the altar, Yahweh’s angel ascended in the flame of the altar. Manoah and his wife watched; and they fell on their faces to the ground.
But Yahweh’s angel didn’t appear to Manoah or to his wife any more. Then Manoah knew that he was Yahweh’s angel.
Manoah said to his wife, “We shall surely die, because we have seen God.”

But his wife said to him, “If Yahweh were pleased to kill us, he wouldn’t have received a burnt offering and a meal offering at our hand, and he wouldn’t he have shown us all these things, nor would he have told us such things as these at this time.”
The woman bore a son, and named him Samson. The child grew, and Yahweh blessed him.
Yahweh’s Spirit began to move him in Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

footnotes.content: How quickly we slip back into what grieves the Lord's heart. Forty years of captivity—that's generations held under Philistine rule. Sometimes our hardest lesson is learning that we cannot drift into bondage without consequence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manoah and his wife—a good man and woman living under the weight of barrenness. They know the longing for a child, the quiet ache of empty rooms. The Lord often meets us in our deepest lack.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An angel appears—not in a vision or dream, but visible, present. The Lord breaks the silence of her grief with a direct word: you will bear a son. Notice He says it kindly, as if He has been watching her sorrow all along.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The first instruction is restraint—what not to drink or eat. Before she holds the child, she must learn obedience. God often asks us to say no to something, not as punishment, but as preparation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Nazirite vow from the womb—set apart wholly to God, from birth to death. And he shall begin to save Israel: what a calling placed on one not yet even conceived. Some children carry the hopes of a nation before their first breath.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She runs to her husband with the news, her words tumbling out: A man of God came to me. His face shone like the face of an angel—terrible and beautiful. She saw majesty and was held by awe. So she tells him what happened, but keeps what she does not know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She repeats the angel's words to her husband: the Nazirite vow, the purity rules, the whole commission. She is stewarding the message carefully, wanting Manoah to know what the Lord has said. This is what faithfulness looks like in a marriage—sharing what God has shown us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manoah prays. He doesn't argue or doubt his wife. Instead, he brings the matter to the Lord himself: teach us what we should do. What a tender moment—both of them seeking God together, both hungry to know how to raise this promised child rightly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angel comes again, but this time only to the woman in the field. God hears the husband's prayer and answers by returning to the wife. He knows whom He called, and He comes back to her. She is the one carrying the news, carrying the child.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She hurries—fear and joy mixed together—to bring her husband. This is urgency born of recognition: that presence, that voice. She has seen the angel again and knows her husband must witness this, must hear it for himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manoah follows his wife and comes to the man. Then the question: Are you the man who spoke to my wife? Simple, direct, seeking confirmation. And the angel answers simply: I am. Sometimes faith needs that one clear word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manoah asks: What shall the child's way of life and mission be? He wants to understand not just the rules, but the purpose. A good father seeks to know what God intends for his child, not merely how to keep him safe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angel's answer circles back to what the woman must do: Let her beware. The focus stays on the mother's obedience. She is the guardian of this child's calling, and her faithfulness will shape his whole life before he is born.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Nazirite rules are restated—no grape vine, no strong drink, nothing unclean. These were the marks of one wholly given to God among Israel. To live under this vow meant to carry a visible, daily reminder of belonging entirely to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manoah offers hospitality: Please stay with us while we prepare a young goat. He is moved to give something—the ancient courtesy of breaking bread together. He does not yet know to whom he offers it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angel declines: I won't eat your bread. But if you will offer a burnt offering to Yahweh—offer it to Him. The angel points away from himself, toward God alone. This is the mark of a true messenger: he draws all honor upward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manoah asks: What is your name, that when your words happen, we may honor you? He wants to know who to thank, who to praise. But names hold power, and this messenger comes from beyond human knowing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why do you ask my name, since it is incomprehensible? The angel's answer is gentle but firm: some mysteries are too vast for us to hold. We do not need to name what we cannot measure or contain. Faith rests in obedience, not in understanding every detail.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manoah prepares an offering—a young goat with meal—and offers it on the rock. They watch together as he does an amazing thing. In that moment, sacrifice meets mystery, and the ordinary stone becomes the place where heaven touches earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The flame rises from the altar, and the angel ascends in it. Manoah and his wife fall on their faces—the proper response when the veil between heaven and earth tears open. This is the moment they know the One who has been speaking to them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angel doesn't appear again. In the silence that follows, Manoah finally understands: He was Yahweh's angel. Knowledge comes not from a name given, but from the mystery witnessed. Sometimes we know God best when we see Him depart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We shall surely die, because we have seen God. Fear grips Manoah—the ancient terror of human eyes beholding the Divine. He has stumbled into the presence of the Holy, and he knows no one is meant to survive that.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But his wife answers with quiet wisdom: If the Lord meant to kill us, He wouldn't have received our offering or spoken these things to us. She reads the sign correctly—He came not to destroy, but to bless. Often the woman sees first what the man fears.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The woman bore a son, and named him Samson. The child grew, and Yahweh blessed him. After barrenness, fruitfulness. After silence, the Lord speaks through a son. Every child is a renewal of hope—and for Samson, a vessel of divine strength.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's Spirit began to move him in Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol. Readers today hear an echo in these ancient place names—the Lord's presence stirring in the ordinary geography of home, not only in temples or prophecy, but in the fields where a boy grows. As of 2026-10, we recognize how near the Spirit remains to us, in the borderlands of our daily lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
